abstracts.abstract: This paper introduces a novel analytical framework that unifies stochastic geometry and deep reinforcement learning for modeling heterogeneous wireless networks in 6G environments. Traditional approaches treat network topology and dynamic resource allocation as separate problems, leading to suboptimal performance in ultra-dense deployment scenarios. We propose a unified theoretical paradigm called Adaptive Graph-Embedded Stochastic Analysis (AGESA), which models spatial randomness and temporal decision-making within a single mathematical framework. The framework employs weighted Poisson point processes to capture multi-tier base station distributions while incorporating Markov decision processes for handover and power control. Through rigorous mathematical derivations, we establish fundamental performance bounds that reveal the inherent tradeoffs between spectral efficiency, energy consumption, and coverage probability under various network densities. Our analysis demonstrates that AGESA achieves up to 47% improvement in spectral efficiency compared to conventional independent modeling approaches while maintaining analytical tractability. The proposed paradigm fundamentally shifts how researchers model the interplay between network architecture and intelligent resource management. These theoretical contributions provide new design guidelines for future wireless systems where traditional boundaries between communications and computing become increasingly blurred.

This paper presents an enhanced analytical model for mobile edge computing task offloading in fog-radio access networks, addressing the critical challenge of optimizing computation latency while minimizing energy consumption. Existing approaches suffer from oversimplified assumptions regarding channel dynamics and task characteristics, resulting in offloading decisions that fail to adapt to real-world conditions. We develop a comprehensive analytical framework based on queuing theory and Lyapunov optimization that jointly considers task queuing delays, wireless channel variations, and variable computational requirements. The proposed model incorporates realistic task arrival patterns modeled as batch Markov arrival processes and captures the temporal dependencies in wireless channels using finite-state Markov chains. We derive closed-form expressions for the achievable trade-off region between average completion time and energy consumption, which enables network operators to systematically configure offloading policies. Numerical results demonstrate that our approach reduces average task completion time by 32% and energy consumption by 28% compared to state-of-the-art methods, while maintaining theoretical optimality within 5% of the dynamic programming benchmark. The analytical framework provides tractable guidelines for designing edge computing architectures in next-generation mobile networks.

This paper introduces EdgeSense, a groundbreaking edge-native network architecture designed specifically for the convergence of sensing and communications in 6G Internet of Things applications. Current system designs treat sensing and communication as separate functional blocks, requiring distinct hardware and protocol stacks, which fundamentally limits deployment flexibility and resource efficiency. EdgeSense breaks this paradigm by proposing a unified programmable platform where radio frequency sensing and data communications share the same physical infrastructure and computational resources at the network edge. The architecture implements a novel middleware layer that dynamically partitions edge computing resources between target tracking, environment mapping, and traditional communication tasks based on real-time application requirements. We design adaptive beamforming protocols that simultaneously support high-resolution sensing and multi-user communications within the same time-frequency resources. Prototype implementation using software-defined radios demonstrates sub-centimeter ranging accuracy and gigabit-per-second communication throughput while maintaining full sensing functionality. The proposed architecture enables unprecedented applications including simultaneous localization and mapping, gesture recognition, and intelligent transportation systems without additional sensing infrastructure. EdgeSense represents a fundamental departure from sensing-as-auxiliary approaches toward sensing-as-native-network-function design philosophy.

This paper presents an enhanced adaptive handover mechanism specifically designed for high-speed vehicle communications in next-generation cellular networks. Existing handover algorithms, originally designed for pedestrian mobility patterns, exhibit severe performance degradation when applied to vehicular scenarios with velocities exceeding 200 km/h, resulting in frequent unnecessary handovers and connection interruptions. We introduce a context-aware handover optimization system that integrates vehicle trajectory prediction, multi-connectivity selection, and intelligent beam management to improve handover reliability. The system incorporates a neural network-based trajectory predictor that leverages vehicle-to-everything communications to forecast mobility paths up to 500 meters ahead, enabling proactive handover preparation. Our design employs a dual-connectivity architecture that maintains simultaneous associations with multiple base stations during the handover region, eliminating the traditional break-before-make approach. Extensive simulations using realistic highway and urban canyon channel models demonstrate that the proposed mechanism reduces handover failure rate by 65% and improves average throughput by 41% compared to conventional 3GPP-specified algorithms. The system achieves seamless connectivity for autonomous vehicles operating at highway speeds while maintaining backward compatibility with existing cellular network standards.
